Comparer.meta_desc: Compare the total cost of ownership (TCO) of all powertrains for your segment: diesel, electric, hydrogen, NGV, PHEV, e-fuel. Incentives, energy and maintenance included.
Comparer.lead: All powertrains side by side — net purchase, energy, maintenance, incentives included. Adjust your inputs and the table recalculates instantly.
Comparer.faq_q1: What's the difference between the TCO comparator and the simulator?
Comparer.faq_a1: The TCO comparator is designed for a side-by-side synthetic view of all powertrains in your segment: it ranks results from cheapest to most expensive and highlights the winner. The custom simulator offers more parameters (per-powertrain purchase price, discounts, detailed usage profile). Use the comparator to decide quickly, then the simulator to fine-tune.
Comparer.faq_q2: Is electric really cheaper than diesel over 4 years?
Comparer.faq_a2: In most B2B scenarios in France in 2026 (medium van, 25,000 km/year), yes: the eco-bonus + low charging cost bring electric TCO below diesel. But the result depends on mileage, usage (motorway vs urban), country and available incentives. Adjust the parameters in the comparator to test your real situation.
Comparer.faq_a3: Maintenance costs are estimated from 2026 industry averages by segment (LCV, truck, etc.) and powertrain. Electric is cheaper (no oil change, no clutch, brakes less worn thanks to regenerative braking). Diesel and petrol include oil changes, filters and timing belts. PHEVs combine both. These values are adjusted by the annual mileage entered.
Comparer.faq_q4: Is NGV (natural gas) relevant for my fleet?
Comparer.faq_a4: NGV (and its biogas equivalent, bioCNG) is particularly competitive for high mileage (> 50,000 km/year) and heavy trucks in France, thanks to a growing station network and a lower fuel cost than diesel. For small or medium LCVs with short trips, electric is usually more advantageous. The comparator lets you see both side by side.
Comparer.faq_q5: Are incentives and subsidies factored in?
Comparer.faq_a5: Yes. The comparator automatically applies 2026 incentives based on the selected country: eco-bonus (France), full BEV tax deductibility (Belgium), cantonal exemptions (Switzerland) and the iZEV programme (Canada). The displayed purchase price is the net price after incentives.
Comparer.faq_q6: How should I read the « winner » badge?
Comparer.faq_a6: The 🏆 badge is given to the powertrain whose total TCO is the lowest over the selected duration, for the inputs entered. It doesn't mean this powertrain is the best in every case: a range constraint, the absence of a charging station on site, or a limited distribution network can make another option more suitable for your situation.

ComparerTrajet.og_desc: Free comparator: diesel vs electric vs hybrid for your car trips.
ComparerTrajet.h1_a: How much will your trip cost
ComparerTrajet.lead: Fuel, tolls, charging stops — compare the true cost of your holiday in diesel, petrol, electric or hybrid.
ComparerTrajet.ped_h2: What this comparator takes into account
ComparerTrajet.ped_1_desc: Motorway consumption (higher than in town). Fuel and electricity prices updated 2026.
ComparerTrajet.ped_2_desc: Real amounts for each pre-filled route. Standard 2026 rates, excluding electronic toll subscription.
ComparerTrajet.ped_3_desc: Number of stops calculated based on real motorway range (~270 km). Charging duration added to trip time.

ComparerTrajet.seo_lead: Cost by powertrain, vignettes, LEZ, charging and checklist for the most popular European routes.
ComparerTrajet.cta_intro: Thinking of changing vehicle? Go further:
ComparerTrajet.faq_q1: How is the motorway charging cost calculated?
ComparerTrajet.faq_a1: The comparator uses the fast charging rate (DC ≥ 50 kW) at public motorway stations, roughly €0.55-0.65/kWh in France in 2026. This rate is significantly higher than home charging (~€0.20/kWh). If you have an operator subscription or mainly charge at home before leaving, the actual cost can be lower. Change the country to adapt rates.
ComparerTrajet.faq_q2: How many charging stops are needed Paris-Marseille in electric?
ComparerTrajet.faq_a2: For a trip of roughly 780 km, with a realistic motorway range of about 270 km, 2 to 3 charging stops are needed depending on starting charge level. The comparator automatically calculates the number of stops and adds charging time (~25 min per fast-charging stop) to the total trip duration.
ComparerTrajet.faq_q3: Are tolls included in the total cost?
ComparerTrajet.faq_a3: Yes, for the 25 pre-filled trips, toll amounts are integrated into the total cost (standard 2026 rate, without electronic toll subscription). Tolls apply equally to all powertrains, so they only affect the ranking if a powertrain benefits from a partial or full exemption (some European tolls exempt EVs).
ComparerTrajet.faq_q4: Is a PHEV (plug-in hybrid) really advantageous on motorways?
ComparerTrajet.faq_a4: On motorways, PHEVs quickly lose their electric advantage: after about 50 km, the thermal engine takes over with consumption often higher than an equivalent diesel (5-7 L/100 km). The PHEV advantage is mostly visible on mixed trips (city + road). The comparator models this honestly: the first 50 km electric, then thermal.
ComparerTrajet.faq_q5: Can I enter a trip not in the list?
ComparerTrajet.faq_a5: Yes. In addition to the 25 pre-filled popular trips, you can freely enter a departure and arrival address. The comparator geocodes the addresses, calculates the real distance via the OpenRouteService API and estimates costs. The distance is an estimate (recommended road itinerary) and tolls are approximated for free trips.
ComparerTrajet.faq_q6: Are energy prices up to date?
ComparerTrajet.faq_a6: Prices are regularly updated by the Moteurs.com Simulator Agent from official sources (DGEC France, European Commission). They reflect 2026 national averages for petrol, diesel, electricity (public fast charging) and NGV. Real prices may vary by retailer and region.

Simulateur.meta_desc: Simulate the total cost of ownership (purchase + energy + maintenance + incentives) across 6 powertrains.
Simulateur.lead: Calculate the total cost of ownership (purchase + energy + maintenance + incentives) across 6 powertrains. All parameters are editable, all assumptions are displayed.
Simulateur.embed_note: The interactive tool below is currently available in French only — field labels (Country, Segment, Mileage…) remain in French. Form translation is scheduled in an upcoming wave.
Simulateur.disclaimer: Disclaimer — This simulator produces an indicative estimate based on 2026 averages. Real amounts (purchase, incentives, energy, maintenance) vary by operator, dealer and your eligibility. Check your situation with a professional before any commitment. Moteurs.com is not a financial advisor.
Simulateur.faq_q1: What is TCO (total cost of ownership)?
Simulateur.faq_a1: TCO (Total Cost of Ownership) is the real cost of a vehicle over its entire use period: net purchase price after incentives, fuel or electricity, maintenance, insurance and taxation. Unlike the simple purchase price, TCO lets you objectively compare all powertrains on the same basis.
Simulateur.faq_q2: Which powertrain is cheapest over 4 years in France?
Simulateur.faq_a2: For a medium B2B van running 25,000 km/year in France, the electric vehicle is generally the cheapest over 4 years thanks to incentives (eco-bonus, regional aids) and low energy cost. NGV often comes second for high mileages. Diesel remains competitive for fleets that charge little or mainly drive on motorways. Adjust the simulator parameters to get the result specific to your situation.
Simulateur.faq_q3: Are government incentives included in the calculation?
Simulateur.faq_a3: Yes. The simulator includes the main 2026 incentives for France (eco-bonus, weight malus), Belgium (100% BEV deductibility), Switzerland (cantonal exemptions) and Canada (federal iZEV programme). Incentives are applied automatically based on the selected country and segment. Always check your eligibility with a professional before any commitment.
Simulateur.faq_q4: How do I change the purchase price in the simulator?
Simulateur.faq_a4: In the left column, the « Real purchase price » section lets you enter the price after dealer discount for each powertrain. You can also apply a uniform global discount (in euros) added to individual prices. If you leave the fields empty, the simulator uses the 2026 catalogue reference prices.
Simulateur.faq_q5: Does the simulator work for Belgium, Switzerland and Canada?
Simulateur.faq_a5: Yes. Select the country from the drop-down menu: energy prices, tax incentives and VAT adapt automatically. Data is regularly updated by the Moteurs.com Simulator Agent from official sources (DGEC, European Commission).
Simulateur.faq_q6: What does « driving profile » mean and why does it matter?
Simulateur.faq_a6: The driving profile (urban, mixed, road, motorway) directly affects consumption. An electric vehicle consumes much less in town than on the motorway, while it's the opposite for diesel. For LCVs, the « mixed » profile is most representative of a typical delivery use. Adjust according to your real-world use to get the most accurate estimate.
